candidate.stem: A commentator argues: "Frontier models will soon have trained on all the high-quality public text there is, so the era of scaling language models is ending." Which assessment of this argument holds up best?

options.text: The premise is well supported, but the conclusion turns on how well synthetic and self-play data work
The argument is sound, since pre-training needs human-written text and the stock of it is fixed
options.provenance: conflates the data wall with its consequence (the FT-8/FT-9 pair conflation), against 'whether data actually constrains scaling through 2030 depends on how well these alternatives work'

options.text: The premise is right but harmless, since images and video can stand in for text with no cap on supply
options.provenance: misreads the multimodal escape route ('could 3-10x the effective data supply') as removing the limit, conflating it with the synthetic-data route the text says could remove the constraint

options.text: The premise is right but harmless, since growth in effective compute can make up for the missing data
options.provenance: misfiles data under Effective Compute, against 'Besides just effective compute, the second overarching factor ... is the amount of available data'

candidate.explanation: The premise is well founded: at recent growth rates, frontier training runs exhaust the stock of high-quality public text within years (the 2024 projections put it between 2026 and 2032). But the conclusion does not follow. Running out of human text closes one supply rather than ending scaling, and whether data actually binds depends on the escape routes: synthetic data removes the constraint only if its quality holds, and self-play works only where a task has explicit rules and rewards. Calling the argument sound conflates the wall with its consequence. Multimodal data helps, but as a bounded multiplier on supply, not an unlimited one. And more effective compute is no fix: data is a second constraint alongside compute, not an input to it. (Forecasting Timelines → Training Data)
candidate.takeaway: The data wall is real, but it ends scaling only if the escape routes fail, so the question is conditional rather than settled.

self_check.cover_test: Yes: a reader who separates the wall from the escape routes will say the premise holds but the conclusion depends on the alternatives.
self_check.cynic_test: The hedged 'it depends' key is a classic tell, so every distractor also concedes or grants the premise, and the one absolute ('no cap') is the multimodal-unlimited belief readers actually hold.
